name: envcheck
problem: Apps crash because a local .env is missing variables that were added to .env.example, or code reads variables nobody documented.
solution: CLI that diffs .env against .env.example and scans source for env reads to flag undocumented variables.
learned: argparse exit-code design, regex-based source scanning, unittest with redirected stdio

name: csv2xlsx
problem: Excel guesses encoding and delimiter when opening CSVs, producing garbled accents, single-column data and mangled ids.
solution: CLI that detects encoding and delimiter and writes a real .xlsx using only the standard library.
learned: OOXML package layout, encoding fallback chain, delimiter detection by row consistency

name: sound-timer
problem: Practice timers count the whole session, so time spent not playing is counted as practice.
solution: Browser app that listens through the microphone and only runs the clock while it hears sound, bridging short rests.
learned: Web Audio API level metering, getUserMedia error handling, separating pure logic for Node tests, timer throttling in background tabs

name: bankcsv
problem: Bank CSV exports differ per bank (columns, dates, number formats, preamble lines), making multi-bank budgeting a manual clean-up.
solution: CLI that detects the layout, normalises to one CSV, applies keyword category rules and prints a monthly summary.
learned: Decimal money parsing across locales, header detection heuristics, inferring day-first vs month-first dates from a whole column

name: logfold
problem: Log lines that differ only by timestamp, id, IP or counter never match, so spotting what a log keeps repeating needs hand-written sed before sort | uniq -c.
solution: Go CLI that normalises variable parts into placeholders, groups matching lines anywhere in the input and prints counted patterns.
learned: RE2 has no lookahead so rule order and word boundaries matter; testing a CLI by making main a run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) function

name: tzquick
problem: Converting a time between zones means a converter site with dropdowns or error-prone mental offset maths; people asked for a tool that takes a phrase like 'today 17:00 Pacific in UTC'.
solution: Static browser page that parses a plain phrase and converts it with built-in Intl time zone data, flagging DST gaps, repeated hours and ambiguous abbreviations.
learned: Turning wall-clock time into an instant with Intl needs an offset round-trip check to detect DST gaps and repeats; keeping parsing in a DOM-free module made it testable under node:test

name: dirdiff
problem: After a backup, restore or reorganisation there is no quick way to tell whether two folders really match; name and timestamp comparison misses corruption and reports renames as a delete plus a new file.
solution: Rust CLI that compares two folders by SHA-256 content and classifies files as identical, changed, moved or renamed, or only on one side, with exit codes for scripting.
learned: Implementing SHA-256 including padding edge cases, avoiding needless hashing by comparing sizes first, and testing a Rust binary through CARGO_BIN_EXE

name: drivecat
problem: Old external disks and DVDs sit in a drawer and nobody remembers which one holds a file; people asked for a tool that indexes them so they can be searched while unplugged.
solution: Python CLI that catalogs file names, sizes and dates into SQLite, then searches, browses, sizes and finds same-name duplicates across disks offline.
learned: A leaked SQLite connection on a corrupt file locks it on Windows, so close on every failure path; storing relative posix paths keeps catalogs portable between operating systems

name: srtfix
problem: Downloaded SRT subtitles start early or late or drift because of a frame-rate mismatch, and player delay settings are not saved into the file.
solution: Node CLI that shifts, stretches or two-point syncs SRT timings, validates cues and renumbers the file.
learned: Linear two-point time mapping for drift, tolerant SRT parsing (BOM, CRLF, missing indexes), node:test for a zero-dependency CLI
